name: SparrowDB
tagline: Append-only image database in Go with a built-in HTTP API and Lua-scripted image processing; idle since 2018.
description: SparrowDB is a purpose-built store for images: each database is an append-only data file of records plus an index file and a Bloom filter, much like the haystack-style photo stores large sites built for themselves. It ships an HTTP API for creating databases, uploading and fetching images (optionally behind random per-image tokens to stop URL guessing), a web admin panel, and Lua scripts that apply image effects on the server through the bild library. It reached 1.0.0 in March 2017 and saw its last commit a year later, so treat it as a small reference design rather than something to deploy.
statusNote: No commits since March 2018 (1.0.0 shipped March 2017); effectively unmaintained. For image storage use an S3-compatible object store with an image proxy.
strengths: Append-only data file with an index and Bloom filter keeps image reads to one seek
Serves images directly over HTTP with no application server
Server-side image effects scripted in Lua
Optional per-image tokens make URLs unguessable
weaknesses: Tiny project with few users and little documentation
useCases: Small self-hosted image galleries or experiments
notIdealFor: Anything needing durability guarantees or replication
